technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Adopt the consumer-side cleanup approach because the admin may not know which Rabbit cluster a stream is deployed to; the container holds that context and can clean up queue/binding/exchange on undeploy.
U1: Use the existing Spring AMQP RabbitAdmin (with getQueueProperties() to detect consumers) instead of invoking the Rabbit HTTP REST API directly.
U1: Treat queue/topic/exchange cleanup as an opt-in flag (e.g., `stream destroy foo --clean`) rather than changing default behavior, to avoid accidental data loss for producers.
U2: Reuse Spring Integration's existing error channel / global error handler pattern rather than introducing a new error mechanism, and expose a tap so external listeners can subscribe.

U3: Use Spring Security integrated with Spring Boot (OOTB auto-configuration where possible) for the Admin server REST endpoints, and configure HTTP Basic as the baseline credential mechanism with hooks for pluggable auth providers.
U3: Apply the same security layer to the Admin UI and require the DSL shell to authenticate against the Admin server (rather than shipping a separate security stack in the shell).
U5: Build a new MVC-aware HTTP source module on embedded Tomcat (Spring Boot) so that Spring MVC controllers, content negotiation, and Spring Security can be leveraged directly.
U5: Keep the existing HTTP source module available for backward compatibility and clearly deprecate it; the new module is the recommended path.

U6: Use a long-polling endpoint on the Admin server (with a future hook for WebSocket/SSE) as the minimum viable client-side status detection mechanism, plus server-side state-change events broadcast to subscribed clients (container + admin) using an internal messaging topic.

U7: Wrap Spring Integration's SFTP adapter inside an XD source module rather than re-implementing SFTP file transfer logic; provide configuration metadata (host, port, user, remote dir, polling interval) consistent with other XD source modules.

U8: Implement the ElasticSearch sink as a native module (using the ElasticSearch Java/REST client) rather than going through an existing generic HTTP sink, to support batching, index/type configuration, and bulk operations.
Cross-cutting: New modules (SFTP, ElasticSearch, MVC HTTP) follow the same module packaging, options metadata, and registration conventions used by existing XD modules.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work, so context-switching and self-review overhead are included in the estimates.
The XD codebase, build (Maven/Gradle), and existing module scaffolding are already available; no greenfield project setup is required.
Java 17+ toolchain is available and matches the runtime target described in the spec.
Test infrastructure (RabbitMQ broker, SFTP server, ElasticSearch cluster) is reachable from the dev environment, but the SFTP test server must be provisioned and the SFTP test harness configured.
Unit tests are required for all new code; integration tests are scoped to a smoke-test level for new modules.
Spring AMQP, Spring Integration, and the (upcoming) Spring AMQP REST API / RabbitManagementTemplate are reachable as Maven dependencies at the version compatible with XD.
No new infrastructure provisioning (servers, CI agents, etc.) is included.
Code review happens through the normal PR/review cycle and is absorbed into the per-activity estimates.
Documentation updates (U4) cover placeholder keys for streams/jobs/containers and reference material for the new modules is added to existing user-guide pages.
Backward compatibility for existing stream/job definitions and the existing HTTP source module is preserved unless explicitly deprecated.

activities.activity_description: Decide between admin-side vs. container-side cleanup, choose the --clean CLI flag shape, design how fanout exchanges are handled when bindings are removed, and document the producer-with-data scenario.

activities.activity_name: U1: Implement --clean flag and RabbitAdmin integration
activities.activity_description: Extend the stream destroy command to accept an optional --clean flag; wire RabbitAdmin (and getQueueProperties() to detect last consumer) so the container can delete its own queue/binding when the stream is torn down.

activities.activity_name: U1: Implement fanout exchange handling and safety checks
activities.activity_description: Handle cleanup of fanout exchanges and bindings where appropriate, and add guards for producers that may still have data in queues to avoid silent data loss.
Unit and integration tests for: default behavior unchanged, --clean removes queue, --clean on fanout, --clean with multiple consumers, and --clean with non-empty queue.
Design the error channel/tap mechanism, decide where the tap is exposed (per-module, per-stream, global), and define the message contract for failure payloads.

activities.activity_name: U2: Implement error channel and tap mechanism
activities.activity_description: Implement a publishable error channel and a tap so downstream consumers/modules can subscribe to per-module and per-stream failure events.

activities.activity_name: U2: Wire error channel into module lifecycle
activities.activity_description: Hook the error channel into the module/stream lifecycle so that exceptions thrown inside a module (e.g., processor, source, sink) are routed to the channel with sufficient context (stream name, module name, exception).
Tests for: error from source module is published, error from processor/sink is published, tap subscribers receive events, no event is published for normal completion.

activities.activity_name: U3: Research Spring Security / Spring Boot OOTB
activities.activity_description: Spike to evaluate OOTB Spring Security auto-configuration in Spring Boot, the relevant starters, and how they map to wrapping the XD REST endpoints listed in the spec.
Design the credential configuration model for users, the auth flow for the DSL shell, and the auth flow for the Admin UI, including how the Admin server acts as the auth authority.

activities.activity_name: U3: Implement security on Admin REST endpoints
activities.activity_description: Wrap all listed XD REST endpoints with Spring Security (HTTP Basic baseline, pluggable user store), secure actuator/admin paths, and add configuration properties for enabling/disabling security.
Prompt for credentials in the DSL shell, pass them on each request to the secured Admin REST endpoints, and handle authentication failures gracefully.
Add a login page and session-based auth for the Admin UI so users authenticate once and the UI can call secured REST endpoints.
Tests covering: anonymous REST access is rejected, authenticated access works, shell auth flow, UI login flow, and that disabled-security mode still works for dev/test.
Enumerate the placeholder keys of the form ${xd.stream.name}, ${xd.job.name}, ${xd.container.*}, etc., and add them to the user/reference documentation as a consequence of not fixing XD-1289.

Design the new HTTP source module: embedded Tomcat, Spring MVC controllers, content negotiation, header mapping, and Spring Security integration points; define the option surface (port, context path, security).

activities.activity_name: U5: Implement embedded Tomcat and Spring MVC integration
activities.activity_description: Stand up an embedded Tomcat instance inside the module, wire Spring MVC, register a controller that adapts incoming HTTP requests into XD Messages.

activities.activity_name: U5: Add content-type and header mapping support
activities.activity_description: Implement richer content-type handling (JSON, XML, form, text, binary) and full inbound header mapping from HTTP request headers to XD Message headers, per the referenced PR comments and SO request.

activities.activity_name: U5: Integrate Spring Security into HTTP module
activities.activity_description: Allow the new module to leverage Spring Security so users can secure the embedded endpoints without rewriting security in the module itself.
Tests for: endpoint receives POST/GET, JSON payload is parsed, content-type is honored, headers are mapped, Spring Security is enforced when configured.

activities.activity_name: U6: Design polling and event-propagation strategy
activities.activity_description: Design the client-side long-polling contract (request, response, timeout), the server-side state-change event bus between containers and admin-server, and the UI notification hook.
Add a common polling client utility (shell + UI) that can be used to detect job/stream status changes during and after deployment, with backoff and cancellation.

Implement an internal event channel that the admin-server and containers use to publish state-change events (deploy/undeploy/start/stop/fail) and a long-polling endpoint that streams those events to subscribed clients.

activities.activity_name: U6: Wire UI notification on top of polling/events
activities.activity_description: Hook the Admin UI to the new status feed so connected UI clients see status changes for streams/jobs without manual refresh.

activities.activity_name: U6: Test polling and event propagation
activities.activity_description: Tests covering: long-poll returns when state changes, clients receive container-side deploy/undeploy events, UI updates without polling manually, no event storms on noisy changes.

activities.activity_name: U7: Research Spring Integration SFTP adapter
activities.activity_description: Review Spring Integration's SFTP adapter capabilities (inbound channel adapter, session factory, polling, file filtering) and the options XD needs to expose.
Design the SFTP source module: option surface (host, port, user, remote dir, filename pattern/filter, polling interval, known_hosts), and the test harness layout (embedded/minimal SFTP server).
Wrap Spring Integration's SFTP inbound channel adapter as an XD source module, emitting one XD Message per inbound file with appropriate metadata headers.
Set up an embedded/minimal SFTP server for tests (e.g., Apache MINA SSHD) so the module can be exercised in CI without external dependencies.
Tests for: new file is picked up, file filter rejects non-matching files, deletion/move-after-read works, auth failures surface as error-channel events.
Design the native ElasticSearch sink: index/type configuration, document id strategy, batching/bulk behavior, retry policy, and the option surface consistent with other sinks.
Implement the sink using the ElasticSearch Java/REST client, supporting indexing of each XD Message payload as a document, with bulk batching and configurable index.
Tests for: messages are indexed, bulk path works, failed indexing is reported on the error channel, index/refresh options are honored.

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting: Integration testing of the increment
activities.activity_description: End-to-end integration tests that exercise the new and changed features together (e.g., deploy a stream that uses the new MVC HTTP source + ElasticSearch sink, verify status via the new polling endpoint, verify REST security blocks anonymous calls).

activities.activity_name: Cross-cutting: Final documentation and review pass
activities.activity_description: Update user/admin docs for new flags (--clean), new modules (SFTP, ElasticSearch, MVC HTTP), security configuration, placeholder keys, and event/poll API; final self-review and code cleanup.
